blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables object-level operations on Gaussian primitives, yet existing segmentation methods are largely trained and evaluated through rendered views. This mismatch can produce accurate rendered masks from incomplete 3D selections since alpha-blended feature supervision concentrates learning on dominant contributors while leaving occluded or low-contribution Gaussians weakly supervised. We propose VODA, a plug-and-play supervision objective that exploits local depth structure to group per-pixel contributors and directly supervises all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, bypassing contribution-weighted gradient delivery. To evaluate volumetric completeness, we introduce Removal-3D, a synthetic object-removal benchmark, and the Removal Depth Error (RDE), a metric comparing predicted and ground-truth depth changes. Across four rendering-based baselines, VODA consistently improves volumetric segmentation on Removal-3D while maintaining or improving performance on LERF and ScanNet. Further analysis shows that VODA recovers lower-contribution Gaussians, while simple gradient reweighting and spatial propagation fail to reproduce comparable gains.
blocks.zh: 3D高斯平板化使得高斯原始人能够进行对象级操作,然而现有的分解方法大多通过渲染出的观点来训练和评价. 这种不匹配可以产生不完全的3D选择的准确制成的口罩,因为α-混合特性监督集中于学习占优势的贡献者,而留下被占有或低贡献的高斯人被弱监督. 我们提出VODA,一个插件和游戏监督目标,利用本地深度结构将每个像素贡献者分组,并直接监督选定的深度集群中的所有高斯人,绕过贡献加权梯度交付. 为了评估体积完整性,我们采用了“清除-3D”这一合成物体清除基准,以及“清除深度误差”(RDE),这是比较预测和地面真实深度变化的尺度。 在四个基于渲染的基线中,自愿官方发展援助不断改进去除-3D的分量,同时保持或改进LERF和ScanNet的性能。 进一步的分析表明,VODA恢复了低贡献高斯人,而简单的梯度再加权和空间传播则无法复制可比较的收益.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Object-level editing of reconstructed scenes requires selecting objects as complete 3D entities.
Removing, relocating, or extracting an object depends on capturing its full spatial extent, including its interior.
For scenes represented by 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) [ 12 ] , this means selecting all Gaussians associated with the object.
Yet existing segmentation methods [ 22 , 24 , 29 , 10 , 28 , 5 ] are commonly evaluated by the accuracy of their rendered 2D masks, which does not establish whether the underlying 3D selection is complete.
Figure 1 illustrates this gap: a selection can produce an accurate mask yet miss some of the object’s Gaussians, leaving visible remnants after removal.
blocks.zh:
对重建的场景进行对象级编辑需要选择对象作为完整的3D实体.
物体的清除、迁移或提取取决于其全部空间范围,包括其内部。
对于以3D高斯镀(3DGS)[12]为代表的场景,这意味着选择所有与该天体相关的高斯人.
然而,现有的分解方法[22、24、29、10、28、5]通常被评估其二维口罩的准确性,这并不能确定基本的三维选择是否完整。
图1说明了这一差距:一个选择可以产生准确的面具,但错过了某些物体的高斯人,在清除后留下可见的残余物。

blocks.en:
This gap stems from rendering-based feature supervision.
Existing methods [ 29 , 10 , 28 , 5 ] learn per-Gaussian instance features through rendered 2D feature maps, using external feature or mask targets, or mask-based contrastive objectives.
Despite their differences, these objectives deliver gradients according to each Gaussian’s rendering contribution (§ 3.1 ).
Dominant contributors can thus suffice to render an accurate mask, while low-contribution Gaussians belonging to the same object receive weak or no supervision and may remain unselected.
blocks.zh:
这一差距源于基于渲染的特性监督。
现有方法[29,10,28,5]通过渲染的2D特征地图,利用外部特征或遮罩目标,或基于遮罩的对比目标,来学习每古西语实例特征.
这些目标虽有不同,但根据每个高斯人的贡献(第3.1节),提供梯度。
因此,主要贡献者足以提供准确的面具,而属于同一对象的低贡献高斯人则受到软弱或没有监督,可能仍然未被选中。

blocks.en:
We therefore study volumetric 3D Gaussian segmentation , aiming to select object-associated Gaussians beyond those needed to render a correct mask.
We propose VODA , a plug-and-play objective that extends object-level supervision beyond the dominant contributors.
VODA modifies only feature supervision, leaving the baseline’s reconstructed scene, feature representation, and inference-time selection procedure unchanged.
blocks.zh:
因此,我们研究体积3D高斯分裂,旨在选择与物体相关的高斯人,而不是制造正确面具所需的对象。
我们提出VODA, 一个插头和游戏的目标, 将对象层面的监督 扩展到了主流贡献者。
自愿官方发展援助只修改了特征监督,使基线重建的场景、特征说明和推断时间选择程序保持不变。

blocks.en:
Our key observation is that, after RGB optimization, Gaussians associated with the same object tend to cluster at similar depths, while larger depth gaps often reflect separation between distinct objects.
VODA exploits this structure by grouping per-pixel contributors into depth clusters and selecting the cluster that best explains each pixel (§ 3.2 ).
Targets constructed from rendered features are then applied directly to every Gaussian in the selected cluster, supervising both dominant and low-contribution members while bypassing the contribution-weighted gradient path (§ 3.3 ).
This direct supervision extends coverage within objects, while a complementary pixel-level push loss sharpens boundaries between adjacent objects.
blocks.zh:
我们的关键观察是,在RGB优化后,与同一对象有关的高斯人倾向于在相似的深度聚集,而更大的深度差距往往反映不同对象之间的分离.
VODA通过将每个像素贡献者分组成深度集群并选择最能解释每个像素的集群(§3.2)来利用这个结构.
然后,通过提供特性构建的目标直接适用于选定组群中的每个高斯人,同时监督主导成员和低贡献成员,同时绕过贡献加权梯度路径(第3.3节)。
这种直接监督在物体内扩展了覆盖范围,而互补的像素级推力损失则会磨合邻近物体之间的界限.

blocks.en:
Evaluating volumetric segmentation requires measuring whether an object selection is complete beyond its visible projection.
Existing benchmarks score rendered masks or visible surface labels and therefore do not directly measure this property.
We use object removal as a diagnostic: removing a complete selection should produce the same depth change as removing the target object itself.
We therefore introduce Removal-3D, a synthetic indoor-scene benchmark with paired ground-truth depth maps before and after target removal.
To quantify how closely a predicted selection reproduces this change, we propose Removal Depth Error (RDE), which compares the ground-truth depth change with the change induced by removing the predicted Gaussians.
blocks.zh:
评价量子分割需要测量一个对象的选择是否超出其可见的投影范围完成.
现有基准分数提供了面具或可见的表面标签,因此不直接衡量这种属性。
我们使用排除对象作为诊断:移除一个完整的选择应该产生与去除目标对象本身相同的深度变化.
因此,我们采用了 " 清除-3D " 系统,这是一个室内合成基准,在清除目标之前和之后配对地面真实深度图。
为了量化一个预测的选题能复制这个变化,我们提议去除深度错误(RDE),将地面-真实深度变化与通过去除预测的高斯人引起的变化进行比较.

blocks.en:
Experiments across four rendering-based baselines [ 28 , 5 , 29 , 10 ] show that VODA consistently improves volumetric segmentation on Removal-3D while maintaining or improving performance on standard benchmarks [ 13 , 9 ] .
Ablations identify direct Gaussian-level supervision as the primary source of these gains, while additional diagnostics support the need to change which Gaussians receive supervision rather than merely modifying the existing rendering-based signal.
blocks.zh:
跨越四个基于渲染的基线的实验[28、5、29、10] 表明,自愿官方发展援助不断改进去除-3D的体积分离,同时保持或改进标准基准的性能[13、9]。
疏导将直接高斯层面的监管确定为这些收益的主要来源,而额外的诊断则支持改变高斯层面接受监管的必要性,而不仅仅是修改现有的渲染信号.

blocks.en:
In summary, our contributions are threefold.
(1) We formulate volumetric 3D Gaussian segmentation, distinguishing selection completeness from rendered-mask accuracy and identifying the bias in rendering-based supervision.
(2) We propose VODA, a plug-and-play objective that directly supervises all Gaussians in selected depth clusters.
(3) We introduce Removal-3D and RDE, a benchmark and metric that assess selection completeness through removal-induced depth changes.
blocks.zh:
总之,我们的贡献有三重。
(1) 我们制定体积三维高斯分解法,区分选择完整性与制造任务精度,并查明在渲染式监督方面的偏差。
(2)我们提出VODA,一个插座和游戏目标,直接监督选定的深度集群中的所有高斯人.
(3) 我们采用消除-3D和RDE,这是通过消除引起的深度变化评估选择完整性的基准和衡量标准。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
The explicit primitives of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) [ 12 ] support object-level selection and editing.
Recent methods attach semantic features or object identities to Gaussians for object-level scene understanding [ 29 , 33 ] .
We focus on how 2D supervision is transferred to Gaussians, distinguishing rendering-based feature learning from direct 2D-to-Gaussian association.
blocks.zh:
3D Gaussian Splating(3DGS)[12]的显式原始支持对象级别选择和编辑.
近代方法将语义特征或对象身份附加到高斯人身上,用于对象级场景理解[29,33].
我们专注于2D监督如何转移给高斯人,区分了渲染学的特征从直接的2D对高斯人协会学习.

blocks.en:
Earlier NeRF methods lift 2D semantics through feature distillation, mask supervision, or contrastive learning [ 31 , 16 , 26 , 25 , 1 , 19 , 6 , 14 , 30 , 2 ] , including distillation of pretrained visual features such as DINO [ 3 ] .
Rendering-based 3DGS methods similarly alpha-blend per-Gaussian features into 2D maps, with two main supervision paradigms. Supervised feature learning matches these maps to external targets: CLIP features [ 22 , 24 , 32 , 34 , 23 , 18 ] , SAM mask identities as in Gaussian Grouping [ 29 ] , or both jointly [ 10 ] . Self-supervised feature learning instead uses SAM masks as grouping cues, pulling features within a mask together and pushing features across masks apart without explicit feature targets [ 28 , 5 , 4 , 8 , 17 ] .
Although their supervision sources differ, these rendering-based objectives share the contribution-weighted gradient path analyzed in § 3.1 .
As illustrated in Figure 2 a, low-contribution Gaussians can therefore receive weak supervision even when the rendered features match the 2D targets or grouping constraints.
VODA complements either paradigm with direct Gaussian-level supervision while leaving the reconstructed scene, feature representation, and inference-time selection unchanged.
blocks.zh:
早期的NERF方法通过特征蒸馏,面具监督,或对比性学习来解除2D语义[31,16,26,25,1,19,6,14,30,2],包括预修视觉特征的蒸馏,如DINO[3].
基于渲染的3DGS方法类似alpha-blend per-Goussian的特征,形成2D地图,主要有两种监督范式. 受监督的特征学习将这些地图与外部目标匹配: CLIP特征 [22, 24, 32, 34, 23, 18], SAM 面具身份如高斯组 [29],或两者共同 [10]. 自我监督的特征学习则使用SAM口罩作为分组提示,将口罩内的特征拉到一起,并将特征推向口罩之间,没有明确的特征目标[28,5,4,8,17].
虽然其监督来源不同,但这些基于渲染的目标与第3.1节分析的贡献加权梯度路径相同。
因此,如图2a所示,即使所提供的特征与2D目标或分组限制相符,低贡献的高斯人也可能受到薄弱的监督。
VODA在使重建的场景、特色表现和推论时间选择保持不变的同时,通过直接的高斯级监督来补充两种模式。

Figure 2: Comparison of supervision and association strategies for per-pixel Gaussian contributors. (a) Rendering-based feature learning delivers contribution-weighted gradients, giving weak supervision to low-contribution Gaussians.
(b) Direct association links each pixel to a sparse subset of contributors selected by contribution-based rules.
(c) VODA directly supervises every Gaussian in the selected depth cluster, including low-contribution Gaussians associated with the same object.

图2:每个像素高斯人贡献者的监督和结社战略比较。 (a) 基于渲染的特征学习提供贡献加权梯度,对低贡献高斯人的监督不力。
(b) 直接关联将每个像素与按缴款规则选定的少数缴款者联系起来。
(c) VODA直接监督选定深度集群中的每个高斯人,包括与同一对象相关的低贡献高斯人.

blocks.en:
Another line of work associates 2D observations directly with Gaussians rather than learning features through rendered-map losses.
Lifting By Gaussians [ 7 ] assigns 2D mask labels to the per-pixel maximum-contributing Gaussian and merges the resulting fragments across views.
Dr. Splat [ 15 ] registers CLIP embeddings to dominant or Top- k k Gaussians for optimization-free 3D search.
Quantile Rendering [ 11 ] uses quantile-based sampling to associate high-dimensional features with a sparse set of influential Gaussians.
Despite their different association rules, these methods associate each pixel with only a sparse subset of Gaussian contributors, as illustrated in Figure 2 b.
Multi-view observations can expand this set, but object-associated Gaussians that remain weak contributors across views may still receive no assignment.
Thus, bypassing rendered-feature optimization alone does not necessarily resolve the incompleteness induced by sparse, contribution-based association.
VODA instead uses per-pixel depth structure to identify the target-associated cluster and directly supervises all Gaussians within it.
blocks.zh:
另一条工作线将2D观测直接与高斯人联系起来,而不是通过渲染图损失来学习特征.
由高斯人提起[7]为每像素最大贡献者高斯人指定2D口罩标签,并合并产生的碎片横跨视图.
Splat博士 [15] 注册 CLIP 嵌入到主力或Top- k Gaussians 进行优化免费3D搜索.
Quantile Rendering [11] 使用基于quantile的采样将高维特性与一组有影响力的高斯人联系起来.
尽管其关联规则不同,但如图2b所示,这些方法只将每个像素与为数不多的高斯贡献者子集联系起来.
多视图观测可以扩展此集, 但对象关联 在各种观点上仍然贡献不足的高斯人可能仍然得不到任何任务。
因此,仅仅绕过成型优化并不一定能解决以贡献为基础的少数关联引起的不完全问题。
VODA转而使用每像素深度结构来识别与目标相关的集群,并直接监督其中的所有高斯人.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
We propose VODA, a plug-and-play supervision objective for volumetric 3D Gaussian segmentation.
We first analyze why standard rendering-based supervision is insufficient in § 3.1 .
The depth-aware rasterizer in § 3.2 then groups per-pixel contributors and selects a target depth cluster.
Direct Gaussian-level supervision in § 3.3 applies a feature loss to every Gaussian in the selected cluster, together with a complementary pixel-level push loss that encourages separation between object instances.

我们提议VODA,一个插座和游戏监督目标 用于体积3D高斯分裂。

§3.2中的深意识光栅,然后将每个像素贡献者分组,选择目标深度集群.
§3.3中的直接高斯级督导对所选集群中的每个高斯级实施特征损失,同时辅以像素级的推力损失,鼓励对象实例之间的分离.

blocks.en: 3.2 Depth-Aware Rasterizer
blocks.zh: 3.2 深度传感器

blocks.en:
To address this imbalance, we need to identify object-associated Gaussians beyond those retained by maximum or Top- k k selection (Figure 2 ).
Instead of relying solely on individual rendering contributions, we exploit the local depth structure of the reconstructed scene.
During reconstruction, cloning and splitting introduce new Gaussians around existing primitives [ 12 ] .
This local refinement motivates using depth proximity as a cue for object association: contributors representing the same local object region can form a depth cluster containing both dominant and low-contribution Gaussians.
Larger gaps can indicate separation from other objects or the background.
blocks.zh:
为了解决这一不平衡问题,我们需要在最大或Top- k 选择保留的对象之外,找出与对象有关的高斯人(图2 )。
我们不单单依靠个人的贡献,而是利用重建后的场景的局部深度结构。
在重建期间,克隆和分化引入了新的高斯人围绕现有原始人[12].
这种局部精细化激发了将深度接近作为对象关联的提示:代表同一局部对象区域的贡献者可以形成一个包含主导和低贡献的深度集群.
较大的缺口可以表明与其他对象或背景的分离.

blocks.en:
To group contributors based on these depth gaps, we introduce a depth-aware rasterizer that collects per-pixel contributors, their camera-space depths, and alpha values.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments

blocks.en:
We evaluate VODA on two standard 3DGS segmentation benchmarks, LERF and ScanNet, in § 4.1 , and on our Removal-3D benchmark for volumetric evaluation in § 4.2 .
We further ablate its design choices in § 4.3 and analyze recovered Gaussians and contribution-based alternatives in § 4.4 .
We evaluate four baselines spanning both feature-learning paradigms in § 2 : OpenGaussian [ 28 ] and LaGa [ 5 ] are self-supervised, while Gaussian Grouping [ 29 ] and ILGS [ 10 ] are supervised.

我们进一步放弃第4.3节中的设计选择,并在第4.4节中分析恢复的高斯人和基于贡献的替代品。

The depth-clustering and loss hyperparameters are shared across all four baselines.
VODA is applied within the existing feature stage for OpenGaussian and LaGa, and as a short feature-only fine-tuning stage for Gaussian Grouping and ILGS.

blocks.en: 4.1 Comparison on Standard Benchmarks
blocks.zh: 4.1 标准基准比较

blocks.en: We evaluate VODA on two complementary standard settings probing different aspects of 3D scene understanding: open-vocabulary 3D object selection on LERF and semantic segmentation on ScanNet.
blocks.zh: 我们在两个互补的标准设置上评价VODA,探究3D场景理解的不同方面:LERF上的开放-vocabulary 3D对象选择和ScanNet上的语义分区.

blocks.en:
Following OpenGaussian, we perform open-vocabulary 3D object selection by selecting a set of Gaussians for each text query and rendering only that set into multiple views.
We compare these rendered masks with the ground-truth object masks from LangSplat [ 22 ] , reporting mIoU and the percentage of queries whose IoU exceeds 0.25 0.25 (mAcc@0.25).
Because selection precedes rendering, this protocol evaluates a single 3D Gaussian selection consistently across views rather than independently segmenting each rendered image.
Gaussian Grouping and ILGS originally produce 2D segmentations by rendering first and then grouping the rendered features.
We instead evaluate them with the same select-then-render protocol as OpenGaussian and LaGa, so their results differ from those reported in the original papers.
Table 1 shows that VODA improves the average mIoU and mAcc@0.25 across all four baselines.
The gains are particularly large for Gaussian Grouping and ILGS, although a few individual scenes show slight regressions.
Figure 4 shows that VODA recovers missing object parts while reducing spurious selections.

我们把这些口罩与LangSplat[22]的地面真人口罩进行比较,报告mIoU以及IoU超过0.250.25(mAcc@0.25)的查询百分比。
由于选择先于渲染,这个协议评价一个单一的3D高斯选择,在视图之间一致,而不是独立分割每个渲染的图像.
Gaussian Grouping和ILGS最初通过渲染先生成2D分区,然后分组渲染的特性.
我们用与OpenGausian和LaGa相同的选择和投降协议来评价它们,因此它们的结果与原论文中报道的结果不同.
表1显示,官方发展援助改善了所有四个基线的平均MIOU和mAcc@0.25。
高斯组和ILGS的收益特别大,尽管一些个别场景显示略有倒退.
图4显示,VODA回收缺失的对象部件,同时减少虚假的选择.

blocks.en:
Following OpenGaussian, we use 19, 15, and 10 ScanNetv2 [ 9 ] categories as text queries and assign each Gaussian to its most similar query.
We transfer these predictions to the ScanNet point cloud and report mIoU and mAcc against the ground-truth semantic labels.
ScanNet complements LERF by evaluating category-level semantic assignment over the entire scene rather than object-level selection from individual text queries.
Table 2 shows consistent improvements for both OpenGaussian and LaGa across all three category splits as the semantic label set changes from 19 to 10 classes.
The gains remain consistent across different category splits, suggesting that VODA is not tied to a particular semantic class partition.
Gaussian Grouping and ILGS are not applicable because their features are tied to per-view SAM mask identities, which the ScanNet text-query protocol does not provide.
Figure 5 shows that VODA produces cleaner semantic assignments around object boundaries, with less label leakage across neighboring regions.
However, ScanNet ground-truth labels cover only visible surfaces in the reconstructed point cloud and therefore cannot directly assess occluded object-associated Gaussians, motivating our volumetric benchmark.

blocks.en: 4.2 Comparison on Volumetric Benchmark

blocks.en:
Standard benchmarks evaluate rendered masks or visible surface labels, but cannot determine whether the selected set covers all Gaussians associated with the 3D object.
In particular, they do not test whether removing the selected Gaussians reveals the surfaces expected after removing the object itself.
We construct Removal-3D, a synthetic benchmark with three indoor scenes (Table, Kitchen, and Room) built in Blender using BlenderKit assets.
For each target object, the benchmark provides paired depth maps of the full scene and the scene after ground-truth object removal.

我们利用BlenderKit资产在Blender建造了Metrole-3D,这是一个合成基准,有三个室内场景(桌子、厨房和房间)。
对于每个目标对象,基准提供了全场和地面-真实物体清除后场景的配对深度地图.

VODA leaves less residual content and better reveals the occluded surface.
blocks.zh:
表3显示每个基线和场景的mRDE持续减少,以及改进后的mIoU。
这一改进贯穿了两个特征学习模式,表明高斯级在清除-3D方面的甄选完整性得到改善,财产标准基准没有计量。
mIoU的增益表明,没有简单地通过扩展所选的组合实现较低的mRDE.
图6对LERF和ScanNet的可视化进行了补充,在删除被询问的高斯人后对每个场景进行渲染.
对于“玩具鸭”和“汉堡”的查询,基线留下了剩余目标内容,表明一些物体Gaussians仍未选定。
VODA留下较少的残留内容,并更好地揭示被渗透的表面.

blocks.en: 4.3 Ablation Study
blocks.zh: 4.3 读取研究

blocks.en: We ablate supervision delivery, the pixel-level push, and target aggregation using OpenGaussian and Gaussian Grouping as representatives of self-supervised and supervised feature learning.
blocks.zh: 我们放弃监督的提供,像素级的推力,以及目标集合,使用OpenGoussian和Gaussian Grouping作为自我监督和监督的特征学习的代表.

blocks.en: Table 4: Ablation on supervision type and pixel-level push.
blocks.zh: 表4:监督类型和像素级推力的偏差.

blocks.en: Table 5: Target aggregation.
blocks.zh: 表5:目标汇总。

blocks.en:
We compare VODA’s direct loss with a rendering variant that uses the same selected depth clusters and target features, but delivers supervision through feature rendering.
Thus, the two variants differ only in how supervision reaches the selected Gaussians.
Direct supervision consistently performs better across both baselines on LERF and Removal-3D, with the largest difference on Gaussian Grouping, where LERF mIoU rises from 12.40 to 43.73.
This shows that identifying the appropriate depth cluster is not sufficient.
Supervision must also bypass the contribution-weighted rendering path and reach the selected Gaussian features directly.
blocks.zh:
我们比较了VODA的直接损失与一个渲染变体,它使用相同的选定的深度集群和目标特征,但通过特性渲染来提供监督.
因此,这两种变体仅在监督如何到达选定的高斯人方面有所不同。
直接监督在LERF和Remove-3D这两个基线上都表现良好,在高斯组中差别最大,LERF mIoU从12.40上升到43.73。
这表明,确定适当的深度集群是不够的。
监督还必须绕过贡献加权渲染路径,直接到达选定的高斯特征.

blocks.en:
We next isolate the pixel-level push loss while retaining direct supervision.
The push loss has little effect on standard LERF performance, but consistently improves volumetric selection on Removal-3D.
This supports its complementary role to direct supervision.
Direct supervision improves Gaussian coverage, while the push loss reduces feature mixing between nearby instances and improves volumetric selection.
Boundary visualizations in the supplementary illustrate this effect.
blocks.zh:
我们接下来隔离像素级的推力损失,同时保留直接监督.
推力减退对标准的LERF性能影响不大,但持续改进了Morech-3D上的音量选择.
这支持了它对直接监督的补充作用。
直接监管提高了高斯的覆盖范围,而推力损失则减少了附近实例之间的特征混合,并改善了音量选择.
补充部分的边界可视化说明这种效果。

blocks.en:
Finally, we compare uniform averaging with the α \alpha -weighted aggregation in Eq. 5 .
Alpha weighting yields modest but consistent improvements across both baselines, supporting the choice to place greater trust in pixels where the selected Gaussian has a higher per-pixel alpha.
Overall, the ablation shows that direct supervision provides the primary benefit, while the pixel-level push improves instance separation and α \alpha weighting improves target reliability.
blocks.zh:
最后,我们把平均值与α-α的加权汇总值进行对比。
阿尔法加权制在两个基线中都产生适度但一致的改进,支持选择在选定的高斯人每像素α较高的地方对像素给予更大的信任.
总的来说,衰减表明直接监督提供了主要的好处,而像素级的推力则改善了实例分离,α-α加权提高了目标的可靠性.

blocks.en: 4.4 Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.4 分析

blocks.en: We next test whether the Gaussians additionally recovered by VODA are precisely those that receive weak supervision through the rendering path, and whether simpler reweighting or spatial propagation can address the same failure mode.
blocks.zh: 接下来我们测试高斯人是否通过VODA额外恢复, 正是那些通过渲染路径接受弱监督的人, 以及更简单的重新加权或空间传播能否解决同样的故障模式。

Figure 7: Rendering-contribution CDFs for LaGa on Removal-3D.

Table 6: Contribution-based alternatives.
Reweighting and propagation yield inconsistent gains, while VODA improves all three metrics for both baselines through direct depth-cluster supervision.

表6:基于捐款的替代品。
重新加权和传播所产生的收益不一致,而自愿官方发展援助则通过直接的深度集群监督改进两个基线的所有三个度量。

blocks.en:
Using LaGa, we compare Gaussians retrieved by the baseline with those missed by the baseline but recovered after adding VODA.
For each Gaussian, we record its maximum rendering contribution w i ​ ( p ) w_{i}(p) over all training pixels and views.
Because the baseline and VODA checkpoints share identical geometry and opacity, as detailed in the supplementary, these contribution statistics are measured under the same scene geometry.
Figure 7 shows that the recovered Gaussians are consistently shifted toward lower rendering contribution on Removal-3D.
At the 1 / 255 1/255 cutoff, the fraction of low-contribution Gaussians is 10.2–15.9 percentage points higher in the recovered set across the three scenes.
The supplementary extends this analysis to six scenes, with accumulated-contribution statistics showing the same trend.
This directly supports our diagnosis that VODA preferentially recovers Gaussians with weaker baseline supervision.
blocks.zh:
使用LaGa,我们比较了按基线检索的高斯人与按基线检索但经增加自愿官方发展援助后恢复的高斯人。

在1/2551/255的截断中,低贡献的高斯人的比例在三场景中回收的套装中高出10.2-15.9个百分点.
补充分析将这一分析扩大到六个场景,累积捐款统计数据也显示出同样的趋势。
这直接支持了我们的诊断,即VODA在基线监督较弱的情况下优先恢复高斯人.

blocks.en:
Table 6 tests whether the imbalance can be addressed without explicitly assigning supervision through depth clusters. Normalize and Clamp rescale the rendering gradient, while KNN propagates features from nearby high-contribution Gaussians.
None of these alternatives matches VODA.
All three substantially degrade volumetric performance for OpenGaussian, while for Gaussian Grouping, Normalize improves LERF performance but severely degrades Removal-3D.
These failures reflect a limitation of contribution-based heuristics.
Rendering contribution alone does not indicate whether a Gaussian is associated with the target object.
Reweighting therefore cannot identify the relevant low-contribution Gaussians or recover those that receive no rendered gradient.
Indeed, across the six analyzed scenes, 8.5–18.7% of recovered Gaussians receive zero contribution in every training view.
KNN avoids this zero-gradient issue, but spatial proximity likewise does not establish object association and may propagate features across object boundaries.
blocks.zh:
表6检验了在没有明确通过深度集群进行监管的情况下能否解决不平衡问题。 规范化和Clamp重新标定渲染梯度,而KNN则传播附近高贡献的特征.
这些替代方案都与官方发展援助相匹配。
所有这三种对OpenGausian的体积性能都大幅降解,而对于Gaussian Grouping来说,规范化提高了LERF的性能,但严重降解了Munction-3D.
这些失败反映了基于贡献的神速论的局限性.
单是渲染贡献并不能表明高斯人是否与目标对象相关.
因此,重新加权无法确定相关的低贡献高斯人,也无法恢复那些没有得到梯度的人。
事实上,在经过分析的六个场景中,8.5-18.7%的恢复的高斯人从每个培训角度都得到零贡献。
KNN避免了这种零梯度问题,但空间相近性同样没有建立对象关联,可能跨越对象边界传播特征.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
VODA closes the gap between rendered-mask accuracy and volumetric completeness by grouping contributors by depth and directly supervising every Gaussian in selected clusters.
We introduce Removal-3D and RDE to measure selection completeness from depth changes after object removal.
Across four baselines, VODA improves applicable standard benchmarks and both mRDE and rendered-mask mIoU on Removal-3D.
Reweighting and spatial propagation fail to match VODA, suggesting that reaching low-contribution Gaussians matters more than scaling rendered gradients.
blocks.zh:
VODA通过将贡献者按深度分组和直接监督选定集群中的每个高斯人,弥补了渲染任务精度与音量完整性之间的差距.
我们采用移除-3D和RDE来测量对象删除后从深度变化中选择的完整性.
在四个基线中,自愿官方发展援助改进了适用的标准基准,同时改进了MRDE和MIOU关于清除-3D的任务。
重新加权和空间传播不能与VODA相匹配,这表明达到低贡献的高斯人比缩小梯度更重要。

blocks.en:
Depth clustering may merge contacting objects or fragment objects with sparse interiors, and the pixel-level push only partly addresses these cases.
Because occluded Gaussians lack feature-level ground truth, we assess their supervision indirectly through downstream selection and removal.
Exact volumetric evaluation requires paired full-scene and object-removed depth maps, available only for the three synthetic Removal-3D scenes.
blocks.zh:
深度集群可能以稀疏的内饰将接触对象或碎片对象合并,像素级的推力仅部分解决这些案例.
由于被包围的高斯人缺乏地貌层面的地面真相,我们通过下游选择和清除来间接评估他们的监督.
精确的量子评价需要配对的全场和取出对象的深度图,只能用于三个合成的去除-3D场景.

blocks.en: A.3 Additional Baseline Comparison and Positioning
blocks.zh: A.3 补充基线比较和定位

blocks.en:
Segment then Splat (STS) [ 20 ] and VODA both seek object-consistent Gaussian representations, but introduce object identity at different stages.
STS partitions Gaussians into object-specific sets using pre-obtained masks and optimizes the scene under this fixed correspondence.
VODA instead operates on an already-reconstructed scene: it adds direct object-level supervision to the baseline’s features while leaving geometry, opacity, and appearance unchanged.
STS therefore establishes object-specific Gaussian sets during reconstruction, whereas VODA improves feature-based object assignment after reconstruction.
blocks.zh:
然后是Splate(STS)[20]和VODA都寻求符合对象的高斯表示,但在不同阶段引入对象身份.
STS 分区 高斯人使用预先获得的口罩进入对象特定集,并在这种固定的通信下优化场景.
而VODA则在已经重建的场景上运作:它给基线的特征增加了直接的物体级监督,同时使几何、不透明和外观保持不变。
因此,STS在重建期间建立了特定对象的高斯设定,而VODA则在重建后改进基于特征的对象分配.

blocks.en:
We evaluate the public STS implementation under the same Removal-3D protocol (Table 8 ).
STS achieves higher selection mIoU than Gaussian Grouping (38.37 vs. 26.23), but has a higher mRDE than either unmodified baseline (62.10 vs. 39.31 and 50.05).
In contrast, VODA improves both metrics for each baseline without retraining its geometry.
Table 8 also reports full-scene reconstruction quality averaged over the three scenes.
VODA leaves these metrics unchanged because it modifies only object features.
In this setting, STS has lower PSNR and SSIM and higher LPIPS than the two baselines.
These results show that reconstruction-time correspondence alone does not ensure volumetrically complete object selection.
However, STS and the feature-learning baselines use different reconstructed scenes, so this comparison does not isolate object assignment from reconstruction quality.
The baseline–VODA comparisons keep the reconstructed scene fixed and isolate the effect of feature supervision.
blocks.zh:
我们评价根据同一《清除-3D议定书》公开执行STS的情况(表8)。
STS实现的选择mIoU比高斯组(38.37 vs 26.23)要高,但mRDE的mRDE比无修改的基准(62.10 vs 39.31 and 50.05)要高.
与此相对照的是,自愿官方发展援助在不对其几何学进行再培训的情况下,改进了每个基线的两种指标。
表8还报告三个场景的平均全场重建质量。
VODA使得这些度量衡保持不变,因为它只修改对象特征.
在此设定中,STS的PSNR和SSIM和LPIPS比两个基线要低.
这些结果显示,仅靠重建时的通信并不能确保批量完成对象选择.
然而,STS和特征学习基线使用不同的重建场景,因此这种比较并没有将对象指派与重建质量隔离开来.
基线-VODA比较使重建的场景固定下来,并隔离特征监督的效果.

blocks.en:
Fixed mask-based correspondence can propagate errors from partial views or ambiguous boundaries into both object assignment and geometry optimization.
This dependence makes reliable masks and cross-view tracking important for reconstruction-time methods.
VODA decouples feature supervision from reconstruction and can be applied to pre-trained scenes, but cannot repair errors in the geometry it inherits.
STS is attractive when a reliable initial object decomposition is available, while VODA addresses incomplete selection in existing rendering-based feature-learning pipelines.
We therefore view the approaches as complementary rather than claiming that either paradigm universally dominates the other.
blocks.zh:
固定的基于面具的通信可以将部分视图或模糊边界的错误传播到对象分配和几何优化中.
这种依赖性使得可靠的口罩和交叉视距跟踪对于重建时间的方法很重要.
VODA脱钩功能为从重建中进行监管,可以应用于预训场景,但无法修复它继承的几何学错误.
当一个可靠的初始对象分解可用时,STS具有吸引力,而VODA则在现有的渲染特性学习管道中处理不完整的选择.
因此,我们认为这些办法是相辅相成的,而不是声称,这两种模式都普遍支配其他模式。

blocks.en: A.7 Real-World Quantitative and Perceptual Evaluation
blocks.zh: A.7 现实世界定量和概念评价

blocks.en:
We evaluate object removal on SPIn-NeRF [ 21 ] (10 scenes) and 360-USID [ 27 ] (7 scenes), which provide captures of scenes both with and without a target object.
For each scene, we reconstruct the with-object capture, retrieve the target Gaussian set with each baseline or its VODA-enhanced counterpart, remove the selected Gaussians, and render the result.
We evaluate OpenGaussian and Gaussian Grouping, using object-mask IoU on annotated views to assess selection.
For a real-world proxy of RDE, we reconstruct the with-object and without-object captures independently using vanilla 3DGS and use their rendered depth difference as the reference removal signature.
Unlike Removal-3D, this reference is estimated from reconstructions rather than ground-truth geometry.
We also compare removal renderings with the without-object reference images using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS.
blocks.zh:
我们评价SPIn-NERF[21](10场景)和360-USID[27](7场景)上的物体清除,它们提供带和非目标物体的场景捕捉.
对于每个场景,我们重建带物体的捕捉,以每个基线或其VODA增强的对应物检索目标高斯设定,移除选定的高斯设定,并得出结果.
我们评价OpenGausian和Gaussian Grouping,在附加注释的视图上使用对象任务IoU来评估选择.
对于RDE的一个现实世界代名词,我们用香草3DGS独立地重建了有对象和无对象的捕捉器,并使用它们得到的深度差异作为参考删除签名.
与Remove-3D不同的是,这一参考来源于重建,而不是地面真实几何.
我们还利用PSNR,SSIM和LPIPS,将去除渲染与无对象参考图像进行比较.

blocks.en:
VODA improves object-mask IoU in all four dataset–baseline settings.
However, the proxy RDE changes are small, with a slight regression for OpenGaussian on 360-USID, and the image-space changes are mixed.
These datasets mainly contain single-object, low-occlusion captures, in which baseline selections already recover most of the depth change.
Moreover, image-space metrics conflate removal completeness with the quality of newly exposed regions, which were not observed during reconstruction.
Thus, these evaluations support transfer to real reconstructions but do not directly establish volumetric completeness under heavy occlusion.

这些数据集主要包含单对象,低隐蔽捕获,其中基准选择已经恢复了大部分深度变化.
此外,图像空间的衡量标准将清除的完整性与新暴露区域的质量混为一谈,在重建过程中没有观察到这些质量。
因此,这些评价支持向实际重建转移,但并不直接确定在大量封闭下体积的完整性。

blocks.en: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
blocks.zh: 神经病 纸张核对表

blocks.en:
1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the
paper’s contributions and scope. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: In the end part of our main paper, we discuss the limitations of this paper. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This paper does not present formal theoretical results requiring proofs. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We will provide open-source codes. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [N/A] Justification: We will provide it later. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The details of training and testing are provided in A.1. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We write them in Appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We write them in Appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The research conducted in the paper conforms, in every respect, with the
NeurIPS Code of Ethics. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [N/A] Justification: There is no societal impact of the work performed. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: Not related. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The models and data used in this paper are open-sourced and authorized. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not release new assets. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: No human-participant evaluation is reported in the final manuscript. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: No human-participant evaluation is reported in the final manuscript. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [Yes] Justification: To polish writing. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.

一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 抽象和导言中的主要主张准确地反映了
论文的贡献和范围。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 在主要文件的最后部分,我们讨论了这份文件的局限性。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 本文不提出需要证明的正式理论结果. 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们将提供开源代码。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:[不详]理由: 我们晚点再提供 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 培训和测试的详细情况载于A.1。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们把它们写在附录中。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们把它们写在附录中。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 本文中所作的研究在各个方面都符合:
神经病 道德守则。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[不详]理由: 所进行的工作没有社会影响。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 不亲缘. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 本文件使用的模型和数据是开源和授权的. • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[不详]理由: 文件没有放出新的资产。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 最终手稿中未报告人类参与评价. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 最终手稿中未报告人类参与评价. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明. 答复:[是] 理由说明: 为抛光写作. · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要的、原始的或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.zh: 索偿

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en:
Justification: The main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the
paper’s contributions and scope.
blocks.zh:
理由说明: 抽象和导言中的主要主张准确地反映了
论文的贡献和范围。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括论文中的说法.

blocks.zh: 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果能够归纳到其他环境。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: In the end part of our main paper, we discuss the limitations of this paper.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 在主要文件的最后部分,我们讨论了这份文件的局限性。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

blocks.en: Experiment statistical significance

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments?

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).

blocks.zh: 对于来自某一特定来源(例如网站)的报废数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。

blocks.en: If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset.
blocks.zh: 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。

blocks.en: For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided.
blocks.zh: 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。

blocks.en: If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
blocks.zh: 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。

blocks.en: New assets
blocks.zh: 新资产

blocks.en: Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper does not release new assets.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 文件没有放出新的资产。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets.

blocks.en: The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used.
blocks.zh: 文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。

blocks.en: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 与人类学科的众包和研究

blocks.en: Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: No human-participant evaluation is reported in the final manuscript.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 最终手稿中未报告人类参与评价.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.

blocks.en: Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper.
blocks.zh: 将这种资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主体,那么应在主要论文中尽可能详细.

blocks.en: According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。

blocks.en: Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: No human-participant evaluation is reported in the final manuscript.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 最终手稿中未报告人类参与评价.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。

blocks.en: Declaration of LLM usage
blocks.zh: 声明LLM的使用

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required.
blocks.zh: 问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明.

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: To polish writing.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 为抛光写作.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要的、原始的或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。
